title: lore read renders markdown in pretty mode; --plain, piped output and --json stay verbatim
description: The operator asked for this directly (relayed by opum-agent, 2026-09-27). Targeted AFTER the 0.11.0 pair; do not start before the release lands. WHY: at a TTY, lore read prints raw markdown. DESIGN (opum-agent call; argue it if the code disagrees): (1) No new flag. Render the body only when the resolved output mode is pretty (stdout is a TTY, no --plain, no --json). plain (--plain and any non-TTY stdout) and json keep the body byte-for-byte, so `lore read <id> | tail -n +3` still recovers it and agents and pipes are unaffected. This mirrors gh issue view (cli/cli pkg/cmd/issue/view/view.go), and --plain is the existing opt-out. (2) NO_COLOR removes ANSI styling only; layout (headings, lists, tables, code blocks) still renders. Frontmatter is not rendered, and the one-line read: header stays. (3) Contract change: docs/reference/cli-surface.md read row (currently line 827, "Plain/pretty is one header line, a blank line, then the body verbatim") is split into verbatim for plain and --json, rendered for pretty, and the read.ts module docstring is updated to match. The LCLI-478 exact-read contract stays unchanged in plain and json. (4) Security: strip terminal control sequences from the body before rendering (the same class as LCLI-249/LCLI-153), so a doc containing ESC sequences cannot drive the terminal. PRIOR ART (verify before choosing): the recommended route is a small in-house mdast-to-ANSI renderer over the already-bundled mdast-util-from-markdown and string-width (devDependencies, compiled into the binary). GFM tables and task lists need mdast-util-gfm plus micromark-extension-gfm, which lore does not have yet. Fallback: markdansi (MIT, 0.3.4, 2026-09-14; its registry deps list marked while its README says micromark, so check which). REJECTED: marked-terminal (unmaintained since late 2024, breaks on marked 10+, pulls in about 5.5MB of highlight.js), ink-markdown (wraps it), markdown-it-terminal (stale since 2022), cli-markdown (GPL-3.0), and external renderers (glow, mdcat, bat) that lore cannot assume are installed. GOTCHAS: width comes from process.stdout.columns (pretty mode only); cap long lines rather than reflowing code blocks. OSC 8 hyperlinks need allowlist detection that fails closed. Legacy Windows consoles need VT processing, so check the win32 builds. OUT OF SCOPE: a pager ($PAGER / less -R); file it separately if wanted.

acceptanceCriteria.text: In pretty mode, headings, emphasis, lists, block quotes, fenced code, links and GFM tables render; in plain and --json the body is byte-identical to the file, and the existing tail -n +3 test stays green
A body containing ESC or C0/C1 control sequences renders with them neutralised (test)
With NO_COLOR the output has no ANSI but keeps its layout (test)
cli-surface.md and the read.ts docstring are updated in the same PR, and bun run lore check exits 0
Recorded outcome: either the renderer adds no new runtime dependency, or each new dependency license and size is recorded on this task

Per opum-agent ruling A (2026-09-28), --plain stays verbatim everywhere, a TTY included. The global --plain help line and docs/reference/cli-surface.md state that --plain emits the body verbatim, terminal control sequences included, and that only pretty mode neutralises them. A test pins both texts

plan: Grounding: lore agent context implementation (reference/cli-contract s1.2/s6/s7.2; reference/cli-surface read row; specs/lore-design s5; reference/architecture s2). reference/tech-stack was omitted by budget and read by id for its s5 parse-only policy.

1. New src/core/markdown-render.ts: pure renderMarkdown(body, {color, width}). Parse with mdast-util-from-markdown plus micromark-extension-gfm/mdast-util-gfm (exact-pinned devDependencies, compiled into the binary like every other runtime library). Walk mdast to text: headings, emphasis/strong/delete, inline code, bullet/ordered/task lists, block quotes, fenced code (never reflowed; over-wide lines capped with an ellipsis), thematic breaks, links as 'text (url)' with NO OSC 8, GFM tables measured with string-width.
2. Security: reuse errors.ts stripAnsiAndControls, applied per line so newlines and tabs survive, on the body BEFORE parsing. No second strip helper.
3. NO_COLOR: color=false drops every SGR sequence and keeps layout (heading markers, bullets, table borders, code gutter).
4. read.ts: pretty renders the body; plain and json unchanged, same one-line read: header. Docstring updated. Width from process.stdout.columns, fallback 80.
5. docs/reference/cli-surface.md read row split into verbatim (plain, --json) and rendered (pretty).
6. Tests force pretty through a hand-built OutputContext {mode:'pretty'}; no TTY dependence.

7. Proof: two mutations predicted in writing first (skip the strip; render in plain too), gates (bun test, typecheck, lint, bun run lore check), compiled-binary size before/after, and a script(1) TTY sample.
implementationNotes:
MUTATION PREDICTIONS, written before either mutation is run. Baseline: 39 tests across test/markdown-render.test.ts (24) and test/read.test.ts (15), all green. No other test file executes lore read (grep: other hits are prose strings only).
M1, skip the control-sequence strip (neutraliseControls in src/core/markdown-render.ts returns its input unchanged; that one function is both the pre-parse and post-parse pass). Predicted RED, exactly 6: markdown-render 'no ESC, C0 ... reaches the output', 'the text around a stripped sequence survives', 'character references that DECODE to a control...', 'neutraliseControls keeps line feeds and tabs...'; read 'pretty neutralises the body's escape and control sequences...' and 'NO_COLOR (even empty) removes every ANSI sequence...' (its fixture body carries the hostile line, so a raw ESC reaches the no-color output). MUTATION RESULTS (bun 1.3.14; bun test test/markdown-render.test.ts test/read.test.ts). M1 (strip skipped): 33 pass / 6 fail, and the 6 red are exactly the 6 predicted (4 renderer AC2 tests, read 'pretty neutralises...' and read 'NO_COLOR ...'); no unpredicted red, no predicted-red that stayed green. AC5 DEPENDENCY OUTCOME. Two new direct dependencies, exact-pinned in devDependencies like every other runtime library here (the npm package ships only bin/; bun build --compile bundles them into the per-platform binaries): mdast-util-gfm 3.1.0 (MIT, unpacked 22,153 B) and micromark-extension-gfm 3.0.0 (MIT, unpacked 20,321 B). They bring 22 transitive packages, so 24 new packages in node_modules and bun.lock, ALL MIT; registry dist.unpackedSize summed over all 24 = 844,658 B (read 24 of 24 rows via npm view). Largest transitive: mdast-util-to-markdown 2.1.3 (189,342 B), micromark-extension-gfm-table 2.1.2 (94,909 B), micromark-extension-gfm-footnote 2.1.0 (79,466 B). Only the fromMarkdown halves are imported (gfm() and gfmFromMarkdown()). COMPILED BINARY (bun 1.3.14, darwin-arm64, bun build --compile src/compiled.ts, exit 0 both times): 85,588,706 B before -> 85,654,754 B after, +66,048 B (+0.08%); bundle 299 -> 383 modules. Serializer check: mdast-util-to-markdown's own error strings ('Cannot handle unknown node', 'Cannot serialize rules with') occur 0 times in BOTH binaries, while positive controls from the same grep occur only after the change ('[image: ' from the renderer 0->2; 'gfmTaskListItem' from the GFM extension 0->4). So the serializer is tree-shaken out and tech-stack s5's parse-only property holds in the shipped binary, although the package is present in node_modules. Rejected per the task: marked-terminal, ink-markdown, markdown-it-terminal, cli-markdown (GPL-3.0), external renderers; markdansi not needed since the in-house route covered every AC construct.

DEFECT FOUND BY THE MANUAL LOOK, fixed before commit. The first draft read process.stdout.columns only when runRead's stdout sink was absent. cli.ts:258 hands every handler context.stdout ?? process.stdout, so on the real path the sink is never absent and a real terminal always rendered at 80. Unit tests could not see it because they inject a sink. A pty capture at 72 columns showed an 80-wide body (93 lines over 72). Fix: read.ts sinkColumns() reads columns from the sink being written to (process.stdout on the real path; a pipe or test capture reports none -> 80). New regression test 'pretty wraps at the width the stdout stream itself reports, and at 80 when it reports none' goes through run(). M3, reinstating the pre-fix line: 39 pass / 1 fail, that test only; restored, cmp identical. After the fix the pty capture at 72 columns: widest body line 72, 0 lines over 72.

MANUAL LOOK (pty). script(1) is refused by this sandbox, so a python3 pty.fork() runner with the window sized in the child before exec (scratch lcli615-impl/pty_read.py; equivalent to script -q /dev/null). bun src/cli.ts read reference/portable-markdown at 72 columns: exit 0, 198 lines, 712 SGR sequences, 0 non-SGR escapes, widest body line 72; saved to scratch lcli615-impl/tty-pretty-portable-markdown.txt. Same with NO_COLOR='': exit 0, 0 SGR, 0 other escapes, widest 72, headings/bullets/quote bars/table rules intact (tty-nocolor-portable-markdown.txt). Piped: 'bun src/cli.ts read reference/portable-markdown | tail -n +3' and '--json | jq -j .data.body' are both 11,621 B and cmp-identical.

FINAL GATES on the committed tree (bun 1.3.14, quest 0.11.0, lore from source 0.11.0, darwin-arm64): bun test exit 0, 4434 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, 17943 expect() calls, 4435 tests across 125 files. bun run typecheck exit 0. bun run lint exit 0: 282 files, 0 errors, 4 warnings + 1 info, all in files this change does not touch (test/ci-workflow.test.ts, src/commands/agents.ts, three other test files). bun run lore check exit 0: 82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 9 out-of-bundle links skipped. bun build --compile exit 0, 85,654,754 B. Mutations re-run on the final 40-test tree: M1 34 pass / 6 fail and M2 36 pass / 4 fail, the same predicted subsets; both restored, cmp identical.

DECISIONS. OSC 8: none emitted anywhere; links are 'text (url)', and an autolink whose text is its URL prints once. Security goes beyond the brief: stripping before parsing alone cannot catch character references (micromark decodes  to CR,  to FF and ‮ to RLO; verified in micromark-util-decode-numeric-character-reference), so every string taken from the tree is cleaned again with the same stripAnsiAndControls primitive (applied between LF and TAB). No second strip helper. The plain path is unchanged, so --plain at a TTY still prints a body's raw escapes verbatim, as it did before; that is the exact-read contract and is pinned by a test. NO_COLOR: emphasis, strong, strike and inline code fall back to _x_, **x**, ~~x~~ and backticked text, so no meaning is carried by color alone (cli-contract s6). win32: NOT measured on Windows. Pretty+color emits SGR only (0,1,2,3,4,9,34,35,36), the same class the existing pretty paths already emit (31,32,33,2,0), so no new VT requirement; a legacy console without VT processing shows raw SGR exactly as it already does for existing pretty output, and NO_COLOR emits none. Layout glyphs are non-ASCII (bullet, box-drawing rules, ellipsis) and need a UTF-8-capable console font. No native calls added.

finalSummary: lore read now renders the markdown body in pretty mode (stdout a TTY, neither --plain nor --json): headings, emphasis, lists and task lists, block quotes, fenced code, links as text (url), and GFM tables, wrapped to the terminal width read from the output stream. --plain, every non-TTY stdout, and --json keep the body byte-for-byte, and the existing tail -n +3 test passes unmodified. Terminal control sequences are stripped from the source before parsing AND from every parsed string, because micromark decodes character references such as ‮ after the first strip. This reuses the shared stripAnsiAndControls rather than a second copy. NO_COLOR keeps the layout with textual emphasis markers. Per opum-agent ruling A, --plain stays verbatim even at a TTY, and the --plain help and cli-surface now say so, pinned by a test. New exact-pinned build dependencies compiled into the binary: mdast-util-gfm 3.1.0 and micromark-extension-gfm 3.0.0 (24 packages, all MIT, binary +66 KB). Verified by 24 renderer tests, 8 read tests driven through run(), and the 2 doc/help tests. Mutations turned exactly the predicted subsets red: strip removed 6, render-in-plain 4, old width line 1, old help wording 1. A parent-side adversarial probe left 0 non-SGR controls. Gates: bun test 4520/0, typecheck, lint and lore check 0. Not tried on a Windows console: it emits only SGR, as existing pretty output does, and needs a UTF-8-capable font for its box and bullet characters.
